evidence: app/nuxt.config.ts:1-18 — no experimental/unstable flags; only compatibilityDate, css, runtimeConfig, app.head
app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:218-220 — useAsyncData with the documented `watch` option (stable since Nuxt 3.6, 2023)
app/app/components/MovesTable.vue:6-13 — plain defineProps/ref/computed, all core Vue 3.5 APIs
app/package.json:12 — nuxt 4.6.3 is the current stable release (2026-10-05), not an experimental channel
reach.rationale: The app is built entirely on long-stable Nuxt/Vue APIs; nothing experimental, preview, RC or canary appears anywhere, and the Nuxt 4 `app/` srcDir layout it follows has been stable since mid-2025.

evidence: app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:212-213 — event.node.res.statusCode is the only low-level (h3-internal) touchpoint, repeated in moves/[name].vue:36-37, abilities/[name].vue:27-28, types/[name].vue:51-52
app/app/utils/poke.ts:48-60 — data layer is a single hand-rolled module; no framework-edge APIs
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain. The one low-level pattern (direct h3 event access) is a fixed three-line idiom copy-pasted across four pages rather than isolated in a helper, but it is stable API usage, not experimental.

evidence: app/app/utils/poke.ts:62-96 — custom fetchApi/fetchRecord/cache instead of reaching for any new data-fetching API
app/app/utils/poke.ts:121-131 — custom mapLimit concurrency helper, no experimental utilities
app/app/pages/index.vue:59-67 — filters implemented with router.push/replace on the standard query, no experimental router features
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, so there is nothing to justify; the app deliberately solves everything with stable primitives, even hand-rolling concurrency control rather than gambling on new APIs.

findings.issue: Sets the SSR 404 via `event.node.res.statusCode` directly (same pattern in moves/[name].vue:36, abilities/[name].vue:27, types/[name].vue:51), bypassing the documented `setResponseStatus(event, 404)` / `createError({ statusCode: 404 })` and coupling to h3 v1 internals that Nuxt 5's h3 v2 / nuxt/server migration targets.
findings.suggestion: Use `setResponseStatus(event, 404)` from Nuxt's SSR composables, or throw `createError({ statusCode: 404 })`, and put the null-check in one shared helper so the pattern is defined once.

findings.issue: Pins nuxt to exactly 4.6.3, a patch release days old at review time; while stable, exact-pinning the newest patch leaves no soak period.
findings.suggestion: Consider a caret range (^4.6.3) with a lockfile for reproducibility, allowing patch upgrades on your own schedule.

findings.issue: Plugin writes to module-level mutable state in app/app/utils/poke.ts:48 (resolvedApiBase), which is process-wide on the server — safe here because it comes from the environment, but it is shared cross-request global state rather than `useRuntimeConfig()` per call.
findings.suggestion: Read the base URL from `useRuntimeConfig()` inside the data layer (or pass it explicitly) instead of a module global, keeping the data layer free of cross-request state.

summary: This app takes essentially zero experimental risk: it runs the current stable Nuxt 4.6.3 and uses only APIs that have been stable since Nuxt 3 / Vue 3.5, with no preview, RC, canary or flag-gated features anywhere. All data fetching, caching and concurrency logic is hand-rolled on stable primitives. The only forward-looking concern is direct h3 event-internal access for 404 status codes, which the Nuxt 5 server migration explicitly aims to obsolete.
